Cloud Execution Engine & Web IDE

The Coralgenz Compiler is an ultra-fast, isolated cloud code execution environment designed for developers, engineering teams, coding academies, and interview platforms. Supporting C, C++, Python 3, Java, SQL, and Web stacks, it delivers sub-second compilation and execution without requiring local toolchains.

By pairing lightweight WebAssembly micro-containers with secure cloud workers, Coralgenz Compiler guarantees zero host bleed, deterministic execution results, and instant stdin/stdout streaming.

KERNEL 01
C & C++ (GCC / Clang)

Standard C17/C++20 compilation with optimization flags and memory safety guards.

KERNEL 02

Fast interpreter sandbox with pre-loaded math, data science, and string libraries.

JDK 21 execution with automatic class discovery and memory constraint limits.

Relational query execution with live visual table renders and query plan metrics.

Sub-10ms Cold Starts

Instantaneous execution lifecycle powered by pre-warmed WebAssembly sandboxes eliminating traditional VM boot latencies.

Process Isolation & Cgroups

Strict memory limits and network syscall blacklisting ensure zero host vulnerability or runaway thread resource consumption.

Interactive Stdin Streaming

Real-time bidirectional terminal input and output handling for interactive CLI programs and user prompts.

Zero Local Setup

Engineers and students run complex code anywhere on any device, from budget Chromebooks to smartphones.

EXECUTION PIPELINE DETERMINISTIC WASM AST

Isolated Execution Loop Architecture

Code is ingested, sanitized, and compiled inside an isolated virtual memory boundary before dispatch:

// 1. Client Dispatches Source Code Buffer
const payload = { lang: "c", code: "#include <stdio.h>\nint main() { printf(\"Hello Coralgenz\"); return 0; }" };

// 2. WASM Worker Instantiation with Memory Cap (128MB)
const instance = await WebAssembly.instantiate(wasmModule, {
  env: { memory: new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 256, maximum: 2048 }) },
  wasi_snapshot_preview1: wasiBindings
});

// 3. Sub-millisecond Execution & Terminal Stdout Capture
instance.exports._start(); // Output: "Hello Coralgenz" (Execution Time: 3.2ms)
